scope: Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests, Temple of Heaven, Beijing
title: Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests
blurb: The Temple of Heaven’s great circular hall in Beijing: a 38 m triple-eaved timber hall built without nails, raised on a three-tiered marble terrace, its dome carried by 28 pillars encoding the seasons, months and watches of the day.

sourceUrls.label: Chinese Academy of Sciences: Temple of Heaven in Beijing
Visit Beijing: Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests

systems.name: Marble terraces
systems.description: The three-tiered circular marble terrace, 6 m high, each level edged with carved white marble balustrades, with the south stairs.

systems.name: Pillars
systems.description: The 28 massive wooden pillars: 4 central Dragon Well pillars (18.5 m, the four seasons), 12 inner gold pillars (the months) and 12 outer eave pillars (the twelve watches of the day).

systems.name: Dougong brackets
systems.description: The interlocking wooden bracket sets, shrinking layer by layer to form the vaulted dome, assembled without nails.

systems.name: Walls and doors
systems.description: The circular timber wall panels between the eave pillars, with doors on four sides. Exact arrangement is schematic.

systems.name: Roofs
systems.description: The triple eaves of deep blue glazed tiles with fascia rings and drainage spouts. Exact pitches are schematic.

systems.name: Dome and finial
systems.description: The vaulted dome converging at the apex, the gilded baoding knob on the Thunder God pillar, and the dragon well ceiling caisson.

systems.name: Floor, altar and approach
systems.description: The marble floor, the central altar platform and the schematic approach of the 360 m Vermilion Steps Bridge.
